name: Lech Koziejowski
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold medal in men's team foil at the 1972 Munich Olympics at age 23, defeating the Soviet Union in the final.
early_history_summary: Koziejowski began fencing at age 13 in 1962 at the Marymont club in Warsaw under coaches Władysław Kurpiewski and Władysław Dobrowolski. He won the junior world championship in Genoa in 1969 at age 20, then competed for AZS-AWF Warsaw and Legia Warsaw before winning Olympic gold in 1972.
family_context_summary: Born in Warsaw to Tadeusz Koziejowski and Janina Makowska; father's and mother's occupations not documented in reviewed sources. Graduated from I Liceum Ogólnokształcące in Warsaw (1967) and later from AWF (1983).
primary_early_advantage_tags: Marymont Warsaw fencing club,AZS-AWF Warsaw,coach Kurpiewski,Polish fencing system,junior world champion 1969
evidence_summary: Koziejowski started fencing at 13 under Władysław Kurpiewski at Marymont Warsaw, a well-established fencing club. He won the junior world championship in Genoa in 1969 at age 20, then Olympic team foil gold in 1972 at age 23. The Polish fencing pipeline (Marymont, AZS-AWF, Legia Warsaw) provided sustained elite coaching and competitive exposure. Family financial background is not documented.
starting_point: Born in Warsaw, Poland in 1949 to Tadeusz Koziejowski and Janina Makowska; family financial background not documented.
current_position: Retired from competitive fencing; works as a PE teacher and fencing coach in Warsaw; living as of 2025.

trajectory.event: Began fencing training at Marymont Warsaw under coach Władysław Kurpiewski.
Won the junior world championship in foil in Genoa, Italy.

family_context_summary: Born to Dora and Nachman Libeskind, both Polish Jews and Holocaust survivors. Family immigrated to Israel in 1957 and then to the United States in 1959, settling in the Bronx.

evidence_summary: Libeskind completed his architectural education by age 26 (Cooper Union 1970, Essex 1972) but had no built work or major competition win until decades later. His first building opened in 1998 and his career-defining Jewish Museum Berlin competition was won in 1989 at age 43. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Giancarlo Baghetti
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1961 French Grand Prix on his Formula One World Championship debut at age 26, becoming the only driver in F1 history to win on debut; also won two non-championship F1 races (Syracuse and Naples GPs) earlier in 1961.
early_history_summary: Born into a wealthy Milanese family, Baghetti started racing production cars in 1955 at age 21 and progressed to Formula Junior in 1958. In 1961, the Italian motorsport federation (FISA) selected him to drive a privateer Ferrari 156, leading to his historic debut wins at Syracuse, Naples, and the French Grand Prix at Reims.
family_context_summary: Born into a wealthy Milanese household; his father was a wealthy Milan industrialist who provided the resources to pursue motor racing from a young age.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a wealthy Milan industrialist; no specific motorsport domain expertise documented, but family wealth directly enabled racing career.
primary_early_advantage_tags: wealthy industrialist father,FISA Ferrari pipeline,Italian motorsport network,privateer Ferrari 156,Formula Junior 1958
evidence_summary: Baghetti's wealthy industrialist father enabled his motorsport career from his early twenties. The FISA-Ferrari pipeline selected him to drive a privateer Ferrari 156 in 1961, and he won his first three F1 races including the French Grand Prix on his World Championship debut at age 26. His family capital and the Italian motorsport network were the dominant early advantages; his career declined rapidly after 1961.
starting_point: Born into a wealthy Milanese industrialist family in Milan, Italy in 1934; father's wealth enabled motor racing from a young age.
current_position: Died on November 27, 1995 in Milan, Italy at age 60; final role: retired former Formula One driver.

trajectory.event: Began racing career in production cars in Italy.
Progressed to Formula Junior, driving a Dagrada-Lancia and impressing observers.
Won the French Grand Prix on his F1 World Championship debut at Reims, the only driver ever to do so; also won non-championship races at Syracuse and Naples.
Signed for the works Ferrari team but his F1 career declined with no further wins.
Left Formula One after his final appearance at the Italian Grand Prix in a Lotus 49.
Died in Milan on November 27, 1995.

evidence_summary: Matyjaszewski followed a normal academic path through his twenties, completing his M.S. in Moscow (1972) and Ph.D. in Poland (1976). His landmark discovery of ATRP, which revolutionized polymer chemistry, came in 1994-95 at age 44-45. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Paul Watson
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Greenpeace in 1972 at age 22 (recognized as the 8th founding member with lifetime membership number 007), having crewed on the Greenpeace Too voyage in 1971 and joined the Sierra Club protest in 1969.
early_history_summary: Born in Toronto and raised in St. Andrews, New Brunswick, Watson was an environmental activist from childhood, destroying animal traps at age nine. His mother died when he was 13, after which he joined the Canadian Coast Guard in 1968, sailed on merchant marine vessels, and became involved in the Vancouver environmental protest scene that led to the founding of Greenpeace.
family_context_summary: Born in Toronto to Anthony Joseph Watson and Annamarie Larsen; eldest of seven children. Mother died in 1964 when he was 13, after which his father relocated the family to Toronto. Working-class background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early activism,Coast Guard experience,mother's death,Vancouver environmental movement,Greenpeace co-founder 1972
evidence_summary: Watson's early life was shaped by his mother's death at age 13 and a deep commitment to animal protection from childhood. He gained maritime experience through the Canadian Coast Guard and merchant marine, then immersed himself in Vancouver's environmental protest scene. Co-founding Greenpeace at age 22 was enabled by the rising environmental movement of the early 1970s and his direct-action maritime skills rather than family resources or institutional pipelines.
starting_point: Born in Toronto, Canada in 1950 to Anthony Joseph Watson and Annamarie Larsen; eldest of seven children in a working-class family; grew up in St. Andrews, New Brunswick.
current_position: Founder and leader of the Paul Watson Foundation Fleet; continues marine conservation activism; living as of 2025.

trajectory.event: Joined the Canadian Coast Guard and gained sailing experience on weatherships.
Joined a Sierra Club protest against nuclear testing at Amchitka Island, joining the Don't Make a Wave Committee.
Crewed on the Greenpeace Too voyage to oppose nuclear testing in the Aleutians.
Co-founded Greenpeace, recognized as the 8th founding member with lifetime membership number 007.
Participated in Greenpeace's first anti-whaling mission against the Soviet whaling fleet, a formative experience.
Founded the Sea Shepherd Conservation Society after being ousted from Greenpeace over tactical disagreements.
Named one of Time magazine's environmental heroes of the 20th century.

name: Oleg Romanishin
milestone_by_age_26: Won the European Junior Chess Championship in 1973 at age 21, became an International Master the same year, shared second at the 1975 USSR Championship, and had his Grandmaster title ratified in 1976 at age 24.
early_history_summary: Born in Lviv, Ukrainian SSR, Romanishin trained at the famous Lviv 'Kart school' under Viktor Kart alongside future GMs Beliavsky and Mikhalchishin. He won the European Junior Championship in 1973, became an IM, then was mentored by ex-world champion Mikhail Tal, leading to his GM title in 1976 and a peak world ranking of No. 11 in 1978.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; grew up in Lviv, Ukrainian SSR, a city with a strong chess tradition.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Lviv Kart school,Viktor Kart coach,Mikhail Tal mentor,Beliavsky and Mikhalchishin peers,Soviet chess pipeline,European Junior Champion 1973
evidence_summary: Romanishin was a product of the Lviv chess school under Viktor Kart, training alongside future GMs Beliavsky and Mikhalchishin. He won the European Junior Championship at 21, earned his GM title at 24, and was mentored by ex-world champion Mikhail Tal. The Soviet chess pipeline and the intense peer group in Lviv were the dominant early advantages. Family background is not documented.
starting_point: Born in Lviv, Ukrainian SSR in 1952; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Active as a chess grandmaster and coach in Lviv, Ukraine; living as of 2025.

name: Naji al-Ali
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Al-Ali's first cartoons were published in al-Hurriyya magazine in 1962 (age ~25) and he began contributing to Al Tali'a in Kuwait in 1963, but these were career-starting publications, not material milestones of recognition or success; his fame as one of the Arab world's best-known cartoonists came later.
early_history_summary: Born in the Palestinian village of Al-Shajara, al-Ali became a refugee in 1948, living in Ain al-Hilweh camp in Lebanon. He trained as a car mechanic, worked in Saudi Arabia, then enrolled at the Lebanese Academy of Fine Arts in 1959. His first cartoons were published by Ghassan Kanafani in al-Hurriyya magazine in 1962, and he moved to Kuwait in 1963 to work as a cartoonist.
family_context_summary: Born to Salim Hussein al-Ali in the Palestinian village of Al-Shajara; family became refugees in 1948, living in Ain al-Hilweh camp near Sidon, Lebanon, in a 10-square-meter tent.
evidence_summary: Al-Ali's first cartoons were published in 1962 when he was approximately 25, and he began working as a cartoonist for Al Tali'a in Kuwait in 1963. While these were verifiable career-starting events, they do not constitute material milestones of recognition or success by age 26. His fame as one of the Arab world's most celebrated cartoonists, and the creation of his iconic character Handala, came in subsequent decades.
